doc.title: Vi Redd interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999

title: Wish to play in a movie and final wrap-up
summary: She wants her saxophone used in a film, mentions Lalo Schifrin and being asked if jazz musicians read music, and the interview ends.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: I’d just like to wrap up and ask you if there’s something that you’d really like to do in the future that you haven’t done yet?

Okay. I’ve done a lot of things you know with that instrument playing and concerts, but I would like very much when I hear my instrument, when I hear me on a record or something, I’d like for my instrument to be used in a movie. That’s the one thing that I desire. And I think that it would be very effective. I’m not saying it in any vanity, but I just want to play in a movie. If just my instrument or even my instrument with other instruments. I just feel that so intensely, and that’s what I’d like to do.
Do you have a picture in your mind of what would be going on?

Something with children, or even a mystery, some kind of mystery. But I hear myself. I’m wanting to hear myself I guess I should say, in a movie. And Lalo Schifrin does movies and I met him when he was with Diz, and I’ve been saying I was going to call Lalo and let him know what my desire is. And often times people will say, “Jazz musicians? Do you read music?” Of course I read music. I had a guy ask me that one time. I was doing a record date for Rahsaan Roland Kirk. And he says, “Well do you read music?” And I thought that was so strange. Of course I read music.
Yes, absolutely. But some people feel like jazz musicians — but hey, I had a heck of a teacher.
Well I hope you find that desire fulfilled.
I really hope that that wish is granted.
And remember, you said women have to be a little aggressive in the music business.
So maybe you should make that call.
Thank you. It’s been a pleasure.
